summary: Verified idempotency fix for Stripe subscription welcome email. Wrote 6 focused tests calling mark_subscription_paid twice for the same session (scenario A polling→webhook, scenario B webhook→polling, scenario C polling-only), plus regression checks. All 6 new tests PASS. send_monthly_discounts_notification is invoked exactly ONCE regardless of call order; welcome_email_sent flag is set on payment_transaction; only 1 active subscription remains; email failure does not break subscription creation; Stripe webhook still rejects invalid signature with 400. Existing test_pin_auth_flow.py: 16/22 pass — the 6 failures are pre-existing test-infrastructure errors (module-level MONGO_URL parsing via open('/app/backend/.env').read().split('MONGO_URL=')...), NOT regressions caused by this fix.

critical.issue: PayPal activation flow does NOT call send_monthly_discounts_notification after inserting the subscription. Review request explicitly asked to regression-check that this endpoint 'continua a mandare la mail send_monthly_discounts_notification esattamente una volta dopo l'inserimento della subscription'. grep of server.py shows the email function is referenced only inside mark_subscription_paid (line 910). PayPal subscribers therefore receive NO welcome email. Either a pre-existing missing feature or a regression from a prior refactor — main agent should confirm history and add the send inside paypal_activate right after db.subscriptions.insert_one(doc), wrapped in try/except.

minor.issue: MONGO_URL is parsed with open('/app/backend/.env').read().split('MONGO_URL=')[1].split('\n')[0].strip() which mis-parses when the env value contains characters or the file has trailing content, producing an InvalidURI in AsyncIOMotorClient. 6 tests that use the db fixture error out under pytest even though the flows work in the live backend. Pre-existing, not caused by this iteration.

action_items: Add send_monthly_discounts_notification call inside /api/paypal/activate right after db.subscriptions.insert_one(doc), wrapped in try/except, so PayPal subscribers also receive the activation email.
(Nice-to-have) fix MONGO_URL parsing in tests/test_pin_auth_flow.py db fixture — read via python-dotenv or shlex instead of naive split, so all 22 tests can run under pytest.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py mark_subscription_paid (L878-912): idempotency implemented correctly with find_one_and_update({session_id, welcome_email_sent: {$ne: True}}). Race-safe.

server.py L954-963: webhook branch also uses conditional update on payment_status != 'paid' and only calls mark_subscription_paid when modified_count>0; the email itself is now inside mark_subscription_paid so the second caller's no-op is safe.

server.py L887 always inserts a NEW subscriptions doc — the old actives are marked 'replaced' first, so double-call yields 1 active + 1 replaced (verified). Not a duplicate for the user, but subscription rows accumulate. If desired, consider making the insert conditional on stripe_session_id uniqueness to avoid replaced-row clutter.
server.py 1726 lines — should be split into routers (auth, stripe, paypal, merchants, discounts). Exceeds 700-line guideline.
server.py on_event('startup'/'shutdown') is deprecated — migrate to FastAPI lifespan handlers.
PayPal activate flow lacks welcome email — see backend_issues.critical above.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The Stripe welcome-email idempotency fix is verified end-to-end at unit level (mark_subscription_paid called twice → exactly 1 email, 1 active subscription, welcome_email_sent flag persisted). The remaining regression concern is that /api/paypal/activate does not call send_monthly_discounts_notification at all — verify with the main agent's fix once applied by writing a small test that patches server.send_monthly_discounts_notification and POSTs /api/paypal/activate with a mocked paypal_service.get_subscription returning status='ACTIVE'. Also consider fixing the MONGO_URL parsing in test_pin_auth_flow.py to unblock the 6 pre-existing test errors.
rca of the issue: Root cause: mark_subscription_paid was previously called by both polling (/payments/status/{sid}) and webhook, but the welcome email was sent from within the webhook's `if modified_count>0` branch. Polling would win the race, flip payment_status to 'paid' first, and the webhook's conditional update would return modified_count=0, so the email code path never executed. Fix (verified): the email send is now inside mark_subscription_paid, guarded by find_one_and_update({session_id, welcome_email_sent: {$ne: True}}) which atomically wins for exactly one caller. Verified via 6 new pytest cases exercising both orderings and the failure-of-email scenario.
